Your resume may be costing you interview opportunities — and you might not even realise it.

Many freshers spend hours applying for jobs but overlook simple mistakes in their resumes.

A good resume isn't just about listing your degree, skills and projects. It should also be clear, relevant, well-structured and easy for Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) to read.

Before applying for your next job, check whether your resume has these problems:

• Unclear or poorly structured information
• Formatting that makes your resume difficult to read
• Missing or irrelevant keywords
• Skills and projects that aren't presented effectively

Even small improvements can make your resume easier for recruiters to review.

At Way2Fresher, we've put together a guide covering 10 common resume mistakes freshers make — and practical ways to fix them with an ATS-friendly approach.
